questions.question: Give the hall-hire relationship (R500 plus R40 per guest) in all six forms.
questions.expected_answer: Words: cost is R500 plus R40 per guest. Diagram: multiply by 40, add 500. Table: 10 → 900, 20 → 1 300, 30 → 1 700. Formula: C = 40g + 500. Number sentence: 40(20) + 500 = 1 300. Equation: 40g + 500 = 1 700, giving g = 30.

questions.question: What is the difference between a number sentence and an equation?
questions.expected_answer: Both are the formula with numbers substituted. In a number sentence every number is known and the statement is checked true or false. In an equation the output is known but the input is a letter to be solved for.

questions.question: How do you decide whether 2n + 2 and 2(n + 1) describe the same relationship?
questions.expected_answer: Expand 2(n + 1) to 2n + 2 — identical, so equivalent for every n. Alternatively evaluate both at several inputs: n = 3 gives 8 from both. One disagreement would prove them different; identical algebra proves them the same.
